name: Canadian Standards Association (operating as CSA Group), including its commercial subsidiary CSA Group Testing & Certification Inc. — the latter under an agreement to be sold to Kiwa Group
headquarters: 178 Rexdale Boulevard, Toronto, Ontario, Canada (corporate head office); US head office at 8501 East Pleasant Valley Road, Independence, Ohio (moving to Brecksville, Ohio, in 2028); European head office in Plattling, Germany
employees: About 2,000 across both organisations per the CEO's own biography; the testing, inspection and certification subsidiary alone employs 'approximately 2,100' per its buyer (Kiwa, August 2026); 11,407 standards members; third-party counts conflict from 808 (Canada-only, Mediacorp) to 3,538 (ZoomInfo)

ownership.notes: Member-based not-for-profit federal corporation (Corporations Canada 350893). Its wholly owned commercial arm, CSA Group Testing & Certification Inc. (CBCA 10558257), is under an agreement announced 28 August 2026 to be sold to Kiwa Group (owned by SHV Holdings, Netherlands) for approximately C$2.1 billion in cash (€1.3 billion enterprise value), subject to a two-thirds member vote in early October 2026 and regulatory approvals, closing targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: CSA Group is the Canadian standards body that wrote the large-scale fire test the battery industry's codes now require — CSA TS-800:24, made a consensus national standard as CSA/ANSI C800:25 and referenced by NFPA 855-2026 — and it is about to split in two: on 28 August 2026 the not-for-profit Canadian Standards Association agreed to sell its entire testing, inspection and certification subsidiary, including the CSA certification mark, the OSHA-recognised laboratory status and the twenty laboratories that run those fire tests, to Kiwa Group for about C$2.1 billion, keeping only the standards, research and policy organisation. BACKGROUND. Founded 21 January 1919 as the Canadian Engineering Standards Association; published the first Canadian Electrical Code in 1927 and has written every edition since (the 26th, C22.1:24, runs to 973 pages and was adopted by British Columbia, Alberta and Ontario in 2025); began certifying electrical products in 1940; accredited by the Standards Council of Canada as a standards developer in 1974 and as a certification body since 28 June 1983 (renewed 5 May 2026 to 2031); recognised by OSHA as a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory since 1992, today at 23 sites with UL 9540, UL 1973, UL 1741, UL 2580 and UL 347A in scope. The association reports more than 3,000 published standards, 11,407 members, 411 standards published in fiscal 2024/25 and '60% referenced in legislation and regulations across Canada' (per its annual report); the commercial arm reports 20 laboratories in 12 countries, about 2,100 employees and around 11,000 customers (per Kiwa). Revenue is disclosed to members only; the only public figures are the sale price, a US affiliate's USD 2.9 million Form 990, and one executive's biography recording a US-and-Mexico region growing from USD 35 million to USD 75 million of revenue between 2010 and 2016. Collection gap: the company's website returned HTTP 403 to every request from this environment; its pages were read through Wayback Machine snapshots dated 2024–2026 and are cited by their original URLs, and the fiscal 2025/26 annual report is cited by title only.
ecosystemRole: The certification body in this corpus's assurance segment and the second source to UL Solutions for the North American energy-storage listing — the laboratory that issues a UL 9540 or UL 1973 certificate under an OSHA NRTL scope and the witness at a large-scale fire test — but its distinctive contribution to the battery chain is as an author rather than a tester: CSA wrote the TS-800 large-scale fire test procedure in 2024 'to fill in a critical gap', turned it into the CSA/ANSI C800:25 consensus standard whose stated purpose is 'an assessment of bankability and insurability of energy storage systems', and saw NFPA 855's 2026 edition reference it as the test distinct from UL 9540A. It also writes the Canadian Electrical Code every three years and so decides how storage, inverters and EV chargers are installed in Canada. Its trade-press record places it among the 'major companies' in battery testing, inspection and certification behind the named leaders (UL Solutions, Intertek, TÜV Rheinland, TÜV SÜD, DNV), which is the registry's definition of a challenger; after the Kiwa sale closes, the tester and the author will be different organisations.

productsAndServices.name: Standards development — the Canadian Electrical Code and a 3,000-standard portfolio
productsAndServices.description: The not-for-profit association's core activity: an accredited, consensus-based standards programme drawing on 'over 1,600 in-house technical experts and more than 9,000 volunteer subject-matter experts', with more than 3,000 published codes and standards in 14 areas of focus, of which the Canadian Electrical Code, Part I (CSA C22.1 — 26th edition, 2024, 973 pages) is the flagship: it has been published by CSA since 1927, is adopted by every province and territory, and sets the installation rules for energy storage (Section 64), inverters, EV charging and the rest of the electrical plant. Standards are sold as PDFs, print, the CSA Advantage three-year subscription and the CSA OnDemand enterprise database; 'View Access' is free in Canada with an account.
highlights: Scale per the fiscal 2024/25 annual report: '411 Standards published, including 63 new standards topics', '20 Research reports', '10 Public policy reports', '71 Education courses supporting over 29,000 learners', 11,407 members; '80% of our standards are currently adopted by industry and 60% are referenced in legislation and regulations across Canada'.

The Canadian Electrical Code C22.1:24: PDF and paper editions at CAD 190, bundles with training from CAD 240, the Canadian Electrical Practice Exam with 'over 2,400 questions' from CAD 95; adopted as the BC Electrical Code on 4 March 2025, in Alberta on 1 April 2025 and as Ontario's 2024 OESC on 1 May 2025 (per Technical Safety BC, Alberta Municipal Affairs and Electrical Industry News Week); the 27th edition follows the three-year cycle in 2027.

Electrical portfolio 'of more than 700 electrical standards', including the C22.2 product-standard series that North American certificates cite alongside UL numbers (C22.2 No. 107.1 for power conversion, No. 280/281/346 for EV charging, No. 62109 for PV converters, No. 340 for battery management systems, No. 350 for thermal barriers in batteries).

Accreditation: 'the largest number of published standards accredited by the Standards Council of Canada' and ANSI-accredited as a US standards developer, which is how CSA/ANSI C800:25 became an American National Standard; a 2022 memorandum with UL Standards & Engagement frames joint bi-national standards work.

Funding of access is shifting to regulators: the Canada Energy Regulator, BC Energy Regulator, Alberta Energy Regulator and Saskatchewan renewed 'a financial investment' in April 2026 for five more years of free public access to CSA pipeline standards, and the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission funds read-only access to nuclear standards.

Internal AI: the 'Standards Assistant' launched in 2024 — '140M documents searched; 7,500+ clause titles created; 518 documents summarized; 180+ draft standards generated' in one year (annual report).
productsAndServices.positioning: In Canada CSA is the standards developer with the largest SCC-accredited portfolio and the author of the electrical, gas, nuclear, bridge and pipeline codes that regulators adopt; its competitors for a given standard are UL Standards & Engagement (bi-national UL/ULC documents), IEC/ISO adoptions and, for the Electrical Code itself, the copy-cat publisher P.S. Knight, which Canadian courts enjoined (2016 FC 294, affirmed 2018 FCA 222) but which the US Fifth Circuit allowed to reprint in the United States on the ground that codes incorporated into Canadian law are 'the law' (No. 23-50081, 2024).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: CSA Store (single documents, subscriptions, OnDemand for organisations needing 'access to 10 or more standards for 10 or more users'), training and certification products, and member dues; government and regulator funding for public access; after the Kiwa sale, an endowment-style entity holding the proceeds 'alongside continued member, government, and industry funding support'.
targetSegments: Provincial and territorial electrical-safety authorities and inspectors
Manufacturers seeking a Canadian product standard
Federal and provincial regulators (nuclear, pipelines, transit)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Priorities for the year ahead (annual report): a new parallel research stream, a first North American credentialling programme, clean-energy standards including hydrogen and ground-source heat pumps, transit and passenger rail (Canada's first national transit and passenger rail code announced November 2025), and advocacy on interprovincial trade barriers (a Vice President, Internal Trade appointed June 2026). The 27th Canadian Electrical Code is due in 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Energy-storage standards — CSA TS-800:24 and CSA/ANSI C800:25 large-scale fire testing, C801, C22.2 No. 340 and No. 350
productsAndServices.description: The documents that make CSA a named actor in the battery safety chain rather than one certifier among several: CSA TS-800:24, an interim technical specification published in 2024 'to serve as an interim guidance' and 'fill in a critical gap in the industry by providing a standardized method for evaluating fire hazards associated with energy storage systems'; its successor CSA/ANSI C800:25 (first edition, 73 pages, USD 350), a consensus national standard in both the US and Canada whose scope is a testing protocol for 'quality assurance and reliability programs' intended for 'code officials, financial institutions and insurers, first responders, developers, independent engineers, manufacturers', with data 'intended to be used as part of an assessment of bankability and insurability of energy storage systems'; and the companion documents C801 (detection and mitigation systems), C22.2 No. 340:23 (battery management systems) and C22.2 No. 350 (thermal barriers).
highlights: C800 tests four hazard classes: 'extreme weather conditions (e.g., snow, freezing rain, flooding, and high temperatures); mechanical impacts (e.g., vehicular collisions and structural impacts); ballistics exposure (e.g., projectile testing); large-scale fire events (e.g., thermal runaway and propagation testing)'; the large-scale fire test is Section 9.7, run 'with all fire suppression technologies switched off in order to ensure complete fire consumption of the BESS enclosure'.

Code adoption: NFPA 855's 2026 edition 'will distinguish UL 9540A from large-scale fire testing as two distinct test requirements' (CSA's own article) and references 'large-scale fire testing in accordance with Section 9.7 of ANSI/CSA C800' (NFPA TIA text); Energy-Storage.news reports LSFT 'becomes mandatory in the 2026 edition of NFPA 855' and that UL 9540A's sixth edition (13 March 2026) 'adds requirements for large-scale fire testing (LSFT) alongside cell and module level tests'.

CSA's stated rationale: 'existing standards (such as UL 9540A) are capable of testing for thermal runaway, but they do not adequately simulate fire propagation scenarios' (Marvin Peng); 'manufacturers and authorities having jurisdiction (AHJs) had requested the development of a test protocol' (Michael Becker).

Uptake by product, per OEM releases and trade press: Wärtsilä Quantum High Energy and Quantum 2 (first, November 2024) and Quantum 3 (2025); BYD MC Cube (December 2024); Prevalon HD5 and CLOU Aqua-C2.5 (April 2025, TS-800); Canadian Solar SolBank 3.0 (June 2025, C800 §9.7); Envision 5 MWh (July 2025, C800); Chint C&I (November 2025); HyperStrong HyperBlock III (January 2026, C800:2025); Trina Storage Elementa 2 Pro (January 2026, C800-2025, certified by TÜV Rheinland); Jinko SunTera (April 2026).

TS-800 'is not a consensus document. It has not been formally reviewed or approved by a CSA Technical Committee' — it was a task-group product under the C800 committee, and the store page for C800 already notes 'an update to this product is available'.

C22.2 No. 340:23 'provides requirements for the design, performance, and safety of battery management systems' — a BMS standard, not a system-level BESS standard, contrary to how it is sometimes described; the bi-national system standard remains ANSI/CAN/UL 9540, which CSA certifies to but does not author.
productsAndServices.positioning: The one North American ESS test method authored outside UL: UL 9540A (cell-to-installation thermal-runaway propagation) and UL 9540 (system listing) are UL Standards & Engagement documents, so C800 gives CSA a standards-side role in BESS that no other certifier has. Its acceptance is now written into NFPA 855-2026 and the UL 9540A sixth edition, which means competitors (UL Solutions, TÜV Rheinland) run CSA's protocol too — the Trina, e-STORAGE KuBank and Sungrow PowerKeeper tests of 2026 were witnessed by TÜV Rheinland or UL, not CSA.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Standard sold through the CSA Store (C800 at USD 350); the test itself sold as a laboratory service by the TIC subsidiary or run by any laboratory the AHJ and insurer accept.
targetSegments: BESS integrators and cell makers seeking NFPA 855-2026 compliance
Authorities having jurisdiction and fire services
productsAndServices.roadmap: An update to C800:25 is listed on the CSA Store; NFPA 800 (energy-storage lifecycle) and NFPA 68/69 deflagration guidance are the subjects of CSA's LSFT Hub articles; after the Kiwa sale, C800 stays with the association while the laboratories that run it go to Kiwa.

productsAndServices.name: Testing, inspection and certification — the CSA mark, OSHA NRTL and SCC-accredited certification (the business being sold to Kiwa)
productsAndServices.description: CSA Group Testing & Certification Inc.: 20 specialised laboratories in 12 countries, about 2,100 employees and around 11,000 customers (per Kiwa), operating under recognition by OSHA as a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (since 1992; 23 recognised sites; scope including UL 9540, UL 1973, UL 1741, UL 2202, UL 2594, UL 2580, UL 347A, UL 891, UL 1558, UL 508A), accreditation by the Standards Council of Canada as a certification body (ISO/IEC 17065, since 28 June 1983, renewed 5 May 2026 to 28 June 2031) and inspection body, ANSI accreditation, IECEE CB Scheme national certification body status, IECEx, EU notified-body designations, NVLAP, and energy-efficiency recognitions from the US EPA, DOE, California Energy Commission and NRCan. The CSA mark (with 'US' or 'C-US' indicators) is accepted as proof of conformity by Canadian and US inspectors, retailers and insurers.
highlights: Footprint per the company's locations page: laboratories and offices in Toronto, Independence (Ohio), Irvine, Alpharetta, Plano, Edmonton, Richmond (BC), Pointe-Claire, Plattling and Frankfurt, Agrate Brianza, Arnhem, Hawarden, Bangalore, Guangzhou, Kunshan, Shanghai, Seoul, Yongin, Tokyo, Taipei, Taoyuan and Singapore; the Chinese laboratories operate as a majority-owned joint venture with China Certification & Inspection Group (CCIC/CSA International Certification Co.).

OSHA's dated record: NRTL renewal effective 5 March 2021; ten standards and a second Cleveland building added 17 July 2024 after assessors 'found some nonconformances with the requirements of 29 CFR 1910.7' that CSA 'addressed … sufficiently'; UL 347A added 25 October 2024; the Singapore site 26 June 2025; UL 2580 (EV batteries) and seven power-tool standards 3 February 2026 — an application filed 30 June 2022.

Mark equivalence in Canada: 'because CSA Group, UL Solutions/ULC, and Intertek (ETL) are SCC-accredited, their marks carry equivalent weight as proof of conformity to Canadian requirements', while 'a US-only UL mark by itself is not enough in Canada' (PrimeCables, 2026); Ontario's Electrical Safety Authority recognises 26 certification bodies' marks and lists CSA among SPE-1000 field-evaluation agencies.

The subsidiary's performance is described qualitatively only: 'our TIC subsidiary … had its best year ever, generating the income required to support and grow our Standards initiatives' (fiscal 2024/25 annual report); one executive biography records the US-and-Mexico region growing 'from $35M in Revenues to $75M in revenues' with net margin 'from $13M to $26M' between November 2010 and June 2016.

The sale: 'cash proceeds of approximately C$2.1 billion, subject to customary adjustments for cash, indebtedness, working capital' (CSA, 28 August 2026); enterprise value €1.3 billion (Kiwa); Kiwa committed to 'maintaining the TIC business' Canadian headquarters, continuity of employee pensions'; CEO David Weinstein 'will remain with the TIC business'; advisers Jefferies, Stikeman Elliott and Freshfields for CSA, BofA Securities, Eversheds Sutherland and Borden Ladner Gervais for Kiwa.

Investment continues through the sale: a 290,000-square-foot US headquarters and laboratory in Brecksville, Ohio, broke ground in March 2026 for completion in early 2028 (USD 9.2 million of new annual payroll, 97 positions), the Guangzhou global testing centre opened January 2026, and a Yongin automotive EMC laboratory in April 2026.
productsAndServices.positioning: A mid-tier global TIC company by revenue — absent from Aventis Advisors' 2026 top ten (SGS USD 8.8 billion down to ALS USD 2.1 billion) and unnamed in UL Solutions' 10-K list of competitors — but the second North American mark after UL and the SCC-accredited certifier with the deepest Canadian code relationship. MarketsandMarkets (July 2026) lists CSA among the 'major companies' in battery energy-storage TIC while naming UL Solutions, Intertek, TÜV Rheinland, TÜV SÜD and DNV as the leaders.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to manufacturers under certification agreements with factory surveillance; witnessed manufacturer testing at the client's laboratory (Gotion's laboratory was designated a CSA authorised testing laboratory in 2021); field evaluation on site; Global Market Access packages bundling foreign approvals.
targetSegments: Electrical and electronic product manufacturers selling into Canada and the United States
Battery, ESS, inverter and EV-charger makers
Gas appliance, plumbing, hazardous-location and medical-device manufacturers
Asian exporters seeking North American and European approvals through the China, Korea, Taiwan and Japan laboratories
productsAndServices.roadmap: Change of control to Kiwa Group targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026 after the member vote; OSHA requires notice 'as soon as possible, in writing, of any change of ownership' under the NRTL recognition; Brecksville completion 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Battery and energy-storage testing, UL 9540A and large-scale fire testing services
productsAndServices.description: The laboratory line that serves this corpus most directly: cell, pack and system testing to UN 38.3, IEC 62133, UL 1642, UL 2054, UL 1973, UL 9540 and UL 9540A; UL 9540A unit and installation-level tests 'at our Cleveland, Ohio facility'; large-scale fire testing to TS-800/C800 'at North Carolina, U.S., and Suzhou, China facilities'; battery electrical, mechanical and fire testing at Cleveland and Kunshan; and field evaluation of installed systems for 'low-volume installed systems and custom-engineered projects'. The Independence, Ohio Distributed Energy Resource laboratory is a '40,000 square foot technology lab' offering 'electrical safety evaluation, megawatt scale fire testing, environmental simulations, energy efficiency verification, performance testing, cybersecurity and grid interoperability evaluation'.
highlights: CSA-witnessed or CSA-supervised large-scale fire tests in the corpus: Fluence Gridstack Pro 5000 at SAFE Laboratories, North Carolina — 'CSA Group witnessed and verified the results' (June 2025); Canadian Solar e-STORAGE SolBank 3.0 — 'witnessed and independently verified by both CSA Group, the testing agency, and Energy Safety Response Group' (June 2025); Envision's four 5 MWh cabinets at 5 cm spacing 'under the supervision of the Canadian Standards Association' with the fire 'persisting over 49 hours' (July 2025); Wärtsilä Quantum 3, 22 hours with suppression deactivated (November 2025); HyperStrong HyperBlock III, five units at 100 percent state of charge, 16-hour burn (January 2026); Jinko SunTera, 'first UL 9540A 6th Edition (2026 Draft) Large-Scale Fire Testing certification from CSA Group' (April 2026).

The witness roster is split: Hithium's 2025 test was 'conducted' by UL Solutions; Trina's Elementa 2 Pro (January 2026), e-STORAGE's KuBank 3.0 (August 2026) and Sungrow's PowerKeeper (April 2026) were witnessed by TÜV Rheinland; Prevalon's HD5 TS-800 test ran 'at DNV's test facility in Texas' with the witness unnamed.

Test-data points OEMs publish from CSA-supervised tests: CLOU Aqua-C2.5 burned '59 hours 10 minutes' with the ignited cabinet above 1,300 °C and the adjacent cabinet at 15 cm reaching 80.71 °C; BYD MC Cube 'peak heat release of 5.43MW' with 'no fire spread between cabinets'.

The LSFT Hub (2026) convenes Jensen Hughes, Hiller Companies, PNNL and the Brighton Area Fire Department and publishes on NFPA 68/69 deflagration control, NFPA 800 and wind effects in testing; a BESS Fire Safety Forum was held at the North Carolina laboratory on 26 February 2025.

Kunshan (opened October 2024, 'nearly 8,000 square meters') tests 'photovoltaic modules and components; grid-tied inverters and Power Conversion Systems (PCS); EV chargers; batteries; energy storage systems' for Chinese exporters; Plattling (16,900 m², expanded September 2024) covers EMC, EV high-voltage equipment and batteries in Europe.
productsAndServices.positioning: CSA calls itself 'one of the few testing laboratories worldwide capable of providing large-scale fire testing services' and holds the authorship advantage on C800; UL Solutions, TÜV Rheinland, TÜV SÜD, Intertek and DNV compete on the same tests, and the 2026 record shows Chinese OEMs spreading their witnesses across UL, TÜV and CSA. The North Carolina LSFT site's address is not published and does not appear on OSHA's recognised-site list.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Laboratory service contracts with OEMs and integrators; witnessed testing at client or partner facilities (SAFE Laboratories, North Carolina; DNV Texas); certificates issued under the NRTL and SCC scopes.
targetSegments: BESS integrators and container makers (Chinese and Western)
Developers and AHJs commissioning installation-level tests
productsAndServices.roadmap: Goes to Kiwa with the rest of the TIC business; Brecksville replaces the 1969 Independence building in 2028 while the 2022 DER laboratory 'remains operational'.

productsAndServices.name: Field evaluation, functional safety, cybersecurity, management systems and data-centre compliance services
productsAndServices.description: Installation-side and system-level services: North American field evaluation and special inspection ('over 20 years of experience') to SPE-1000, SPE-3000, NFPA 791 and UL 508A for 'distributed generation, energy storage systems, PV, and microgrid systems', with a serialised CSA label applied on site; functional-safety evaluation to IEC 61508, IEC 61511, ISO 26262 and UL/CSA 60730 'since the release of the first edition of IEC 61508 in 2001'; cybersecurity testing to IEC 62443, UL 2900, ETSI EN 303 645, EN 18031 and the EU Radio Equipment Directive; ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 management-system certification; and a 'Data Center Compliance & Evaluation Services' line applying 'system-level compliance and field evaluation expertise to address installation-specific conditions commonly encountered in mission-critical data center environments' for IT equipment, power and cable systems and HVAC.
highlights: Field evaluation is the route by which a one-off or imported energy-storage installation gets an accepted mark in Canada without full certification — Ontario's limit is fewer than 500 units per model per inspection body.

The data-centre service page offers new-product-introduction evaluations, performance testing, EMC, wireless, functional safety and cybersecurity assessment for OEMs, engineers and MEP contractors; no specific data-centre engagement is reported by any third party.

Functional safety and cybersecurity are the services CSA lists for 'energy storage, smart grids, building automation' — the layer IEC 62443-certified controls (Prevalon's differentiation in this corpus) are evaluated against.
productsAndServices.positioning: Commodity services where CSA competes with every SCC-recognised field-evaluation agency (26 marks recognised by Ontario's ESA) and the global functional-safety houses (TÜV, exida, UL); the data-centre line is a marketing category rather than a documented book of work.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct service contracts; goes to Kiwa with the TIC business.
targetSegments: Data-centre equipment OEMs and MEP contractors
Owners of custom or imported installations needing a field label
productsAndServices.roadmap: No announced roadmap beyond the sale.

productsAndServices.name: Global market access and product-area certification — EV charging, PV and inverters, fuel cells and hydrogen, hazardous locations, EMC
productsAndServices.description: The certification lines adjacent to storage: EV supply equipment to UL 2202/CSA C22.2 No. 346, UL 2594/No. 280 and UL 2231, with vehicle-to-grid interoperability to UL 1741 SB, IEEE 1547.1 and CSA C22.3 No. 9; photovoltaic modules and trackers to UL 1703, IEC/UL 61730 and 61215, UL 3703 and IEC 62817; inverters to UL 1741, UL/IEC 62109 and C22.2 No. 107.1 as an IEC 62109 CB test laboratory; fuel-cell power systems to ANSI/CSA FC1 and FC3 ('the world's first standard for fuel cells in 1998'); hazardous-location equipment under IECEx and ATEX; EMC and radio testing at Plattling, Yongin and Kunshan; and Global Market Access packages promising 'certification services to help you access up to 200 countries' through '34 offices across 13 countries' and 'laboratories and recognized affiliates in over 25 countries'.
highlights: Hydrogen: CSA is committee manager for ISO/TC 197/SC 1, published the CSA/ANSI R124:25 / BNQ 1789-200 harmonised hydrogen carbon-intensity reporting methodology in May 2025 with Québec, SCC and NRCan support, and runs a Hydrogen Fuel System Inspector certification.

EV: NRTL scope gained UL 2580 (EV batteries) on 3 February 2026; the Yongin, Korea automotive EMC laboratory (April 2026) tests 'ICCU, LDC, OBC, BMS' high-voltage components; CSA authored the C22.2 No. 280 and No. 282 installation requirements the Canadian Electrical Code references and is developing wireless-charging standards (C22.2 No. 317).
Global Market Access added a 'service for Mexico and other Latin American countries' in November 2025 and publishes a 'Navigating Tariffs and Global Certification' resource for exporters.
productsAndServices.positioning: The one-stop-shop pitch — 'our accreditations and recognitions make us a one-stop solution for testing & certifying products for markets around the globe' — against UL Solutions, Intertek, TÜV SÜD, TÜV Rheinland and SGS, all of which are larger and hold the same CB Scheme recognitions.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct certification agreements and GMA project fees; goes to Kiwa with the TIC business.
targetSegments: PV module, tracker and inverter manufacturers
productsAndServices.roadmap: No announced roadmap beyond the sale and the new laboratories.

productsAndServices.name: Research, public policy and education — the CSA Research Centre, Public Policy Centre and learning programmes
productsAndServices.description: The activities the association keeps after the sale and that the sale is meant to fund: a Core and an Explore research programme with a library of 185 reports (fiscal 2024/25 topics included recovering lithium and rare-earth elements from waste, smart manufacturing and climate-smart circularity), the CSA Public Policy Centre ('10 new public policy reports' including 'Chip Shot: A Semiconductor Strategy for Canada' and 'Aging Canada 2040', an annual Policy Pathways conference, a government-relations team registered as an in-house lobbyist), and education (71 courses, 29,000 learners, professional certifications for EV technicians and hydrogen fuel-system inspectors, a first North American credentialling programme).
highlights: Energy-sector framing in the annual report: 'our wind, solar and storage capacity is now more than 24 gigawatts, which includes a 92% increase in capacity of solar energy, a 35% increase of wind energy, and a 192% increase of energy storage capacity over the past five years'.

Advocacy focus: interprovincial trade barriers ('could add as much as $200 billion to the Canadian economy'), digital-services trade and AI, and 'a renewed sense of patriotism across Canada' after the 2025 tariff shock — the association's own words.

The post-sale plan: proceeds 'placed in a newly-formed, dedicated legal entity that is wholly-owned by, but governed separately from, the Canadian Standards Association' as 'a diversified, lower-risk source of funding for the standards activities'.
productsAndServices.positioning: In Canada the nearest comparables are the Standards Council of Canada (the accreditor, not a developer), ULC Standards, BNQ and the provincial code bodies; the policy centre competes for attention with think tanks rather than certifiers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Member dues, course fees, government contribution agreements and, after the sale, investment income from the C$2.1 billion.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mary Cianchetti, President of Standards, to become President and CEO of the Canadian Standards Association at the sale's close; a new parallel research stream and the credentialling programme are the stated priorities.

policyExposure.exposure: CSA is an author inside the regime rather than a regulated party: NFPA 855's 2026 edition makes large-scale fire testing mandatory and references 'large-scale fire testing in accordance with Section 9.7 of ANSI/CSA C800', and UL 9540A's sixth edition (13 March 2026) 'adds requirements for large-scale fire testing (LSFT) alongside cell and module level tests'. CSA's own statement is that NFPA 855 'will distinguish UL 9540A from large-scale fire testing as two distinct test requirements' and that 'TS-800 basically mirrors what's in that 855 material'; its staff sit on NFPA 855 and the UL 9540 and 9540A standards technical panels. In Canada the Electrical Code's Section 64 was drafted with NFPA 855 in view and NFPA 855 applies by reference, not by provincial adoption.
policyExposure.mitigation: CSA's stated response is to keep the protocol current — an update to C800:25 is already listed — and to run the LSFT Hub with AHJs, fire services and consultants.

policyExposure.exposure: The testing subsidiary's US certification business exists under OSHA's recognition of CSA Group Testing & Certification Inc. as a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (renewed effective 5 March 2021; 23 sites; UL 9540, UL 1973, UL 1741, UL 2580 and UL 347A in scope). The recognition carries the condition that 'CSA must inform OSHA as soon as possible, in writing, of any change of ownership' — which the Kiwa sale triggers — and OSHA's 2023 site review 'found some nonconformances with the requirements of 29 CFR 1910.7' at the second Cleveland building, resolved before the 2024 grant.
policyExposure.mitigation: Kiwa has committed to 'maintaining the TIC business' Canadian headquarters' and the sale is conditioned on regulatory approvals; neither party has published its OSHA notification.

policyExposure.regime: Crown copyright and the government-edicts doctrine (Canadian Electrical Code)
policyExposure.exposure: CSA's revenue from the Canadian Electrical Code rests on copyright in a code that provinces adopt into law. Canadian courts upheld that copyright against P.S. Knight's copy-cat edition (2016 FC 294; 2018 FCA 222, which held the Code 'is not itself a regulation'; Supreme Court leave dismissed 23 May 2019) and jailed-in-principle the publisher for contempt (2021 FC 1346: six months suspended, a C$100,000 fine and C$50,000 costs). In the United States the Fifth Circuit reversed CSA's summary judgment in 2024, holding that all seven codes 'fully incorporated by reference into at least one Canadian statute or regulation' are 'the law' and copyable under Veeck; on remand Knight recovered only USD 1,707.35 in costs (August 2025).
policyExposure.mitigation: Regulators now pay for public access — the Canada Energy Regulator and provincial regulators fund free pipeline standards (renewed April 2026) and the CNSC funds nuclear-standard access — and 'View Access' is free in Canada with an account; the post-sale endowment is designed to reduce dependence on document sales.

policyExposure.regime: Canadian Electrical Code adoption (provincial and territorial)
policyExposure.exposure: The 26th edition (C22.1:24) was adopted as the BC Electrical Code effective 4 March 2025, in Alberta on 1 April 2025 and as Ontario's 2024 Electrical Safety Code on 1 May 2025; adoption by every province and territory on a three-year cycle is what makes CSA's code the installation law for energy storage, inverters and EV chargers in Canada. Ontario's Electrical Safety Authority treats the CSA mark as one of 26 recognised marks — 'their marks carry equivalent weight as proof of conformity to Canadian requirements' — so the code, not the mark, is the exclusive asset.

policyExposure.regime: Standards Council of Canada accreditation and federal funding
policyExposure.exposure: The association is SCC-accredited as a standards developer (since 1974) and the subsidiary as a certification body (ISO/IEC 17065, since 1983, renewed 5 May 2026 to 2031); the SCC 'has had discussions regarding funding to be provided to Standards Development Organizations, including Canadian Standards Association' (lobby registry), and the hydrogen carbon-intensity standard was funded by Québec, the SCC and NRCan. The 2025 tariff shock is acknowledged in the annual report as forcing the organisation 'to reconsider long-held assumptions about the economy, global trade and international relations'.
policyExposure.mitigation: A Vice President, Internal Trade was appointed in June 2026 to pursue the elimination of interprovincial trade barriers; Global Market Access publishes a 'Navigating Tariffs and Global Certification' resource.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that the Kiwa sale separates the two things this corpus wanted from CSA Group — the author of the battery fire-test standard and the laboratory that runs it — and that after closing 'CSA Group' will be a standards body while the CSA mark, the NRTL recognition and the twenty laboratories belong to a Dutch family-owned TIC group. Basis: the 28 August 2026 release names the seller as the association and the asset as 'the TIC business, a large commercial subsidiary'; Kiwa's release lists the OSHA NRTL status and SCC accreditation among what it is buying; Mary Cianchetti becomes CEO of the association and David Weinstein 'will remain with the TIC business'. The corpus's assurance segment will need to decide at the first refresh whether the challenger is the association or Kiwa's CSA unit.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that CSA's position in battery-storage assurance is that of a challenger to UL Solutions — the second North American source for a UL 9540 or UL 1973 listing and one witness among three for large-scale fire tests — and not a leader. Basis: MarketsandMarkets names UL Solutions, Intertek, TÜV Rheinland, TÜV SÜD and DNV as the leading players and CSA among the majors; UL Solutions' 10-K does not list CSA among its competitors; Aventis Advisors' 2026 top ten by revenue omits it; and the 2025–2026 witness roster splits between CSA (Wärtsilä, BYD, CLOU, Canadian Solar, Fluence, Envision, HyperStrong, Jinko), UL Solutions (Hithium, Sungrow SBH) and TÜV Rheinland (Trina, e-STORAGE KuBank, Sungrow PowerKeeper). That is the registry's challenger definition — a second source contesting the established set.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that CSA's distinctive asset in this chain is authorship — TS-800 in 2024, C800:25 in 2025, and the NFPA 855-2026 and UL 9540A sixth-edition references to large-scale fire testing — and that the sale strips that asset of its laboratory. Basis: C800's scope names 'financial institutions and insurers' and 'bankability and insurability' as its purpose, which is the insurance segment's buying criterion written into a test standard; the repeat customers (Wärtsilä, Canadian Solar) came to CSA because it owned the protocol and the site; after the split the association keeps the protocol and no site. Whether Kiwa's CSA unit keeps preferential access to the standard's development is not stated.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the authorship advantage is already eroding into an industry procedure that competitors run. Basis: Trina's January 2026 C800 test was certified by TÜV Rheinland; e-STORAGE's August 2026 KuBank test went to TÜV Rheinland after CSA witnessed its SolBank test in 2025; Prevalon ran TS-800 at DNV's Texas site; and UL 9540A's sixth edition now carries LSFT requirements of its own. A test written into the code belongs to everyone who can run it.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the Knight litigation matters more for the standards business model than its Canadian wins suggest. Basis: Canadian courts enforced CSA's copyright in the Electrical Code all the way to a contempt sentence, but the Fifth Circuit held in 2024 that codes incorporated into Canadian law are 'the law' and freely copyable in the United States; regulators (CER, CNSC) now pay CSA for free public access rather than the public paying for documents; and the sale's stated purpose is 'a financial foundation that is not exposed to the pressures of a large commercial business'. The endowment replaces document sales as the funding logic.

6. **(High confidence)** We assess that CSA's home-market moat is the code, not the mark. Basis: Ontario's ESA recognises 26 certification marks and third-party guidance states that SCC-accredited marks 'carry equivalent weight as proof of conformity'; the one asymmetry — 'a US-only UL mark by itself is not enough in Canada' — favours every SCC-accredited body equally. What only CSA has is the Canadian Electrical Code and the three-year cycle that puts storage (Section 64), EV charging and inverters into provincial law.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess that Kiwa ownership will keep the North American laboratories investing but shift the unit's strategic centre toward Europe. Basis: Kiwa's commitments cover the Canadian headquarters and pensions, and the Brecksville build was already funded; against this, Kiwa is a 12,000-person European group and the CSA unit's growth capital of the last two years went to Kunshan, Plattling, Yongin and Guangzhou. This is inference from ownership; no party has said it.

Collection gap: www.csagroup.org returned HTTP 403 to every request (three samples on each of five paths, two user agents, and the harness fetcher), so the company's pages were read from Wayback Machine snapshots dated 2024–2026 and are cited by their original URLs; the fiscal 2025/26 annual report and the 2026 news releases have no archive capture and are cited by title. Revenue, surplus and segment figures are members-only. The North Carolina large-scale fire test site's address and ownership, the fiscal year-end date, and the fate of the CCIC joint venture under Kiwa are not published. Third parties disagree on headcount (808, about 2,100, 3,538) because they count different entities.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Early October 2026 — the special meeting of members:* a two-thirds vote for the sale confirms Judgment 1; a failed vote leaves the group intact and this dossier's structure current. *Fourth quarter 2026 — closing:* the OSHA change-of-ownership notice and any renaming of the CSA mark or of CSA Group Testing & Certification Inc. would show what Kiwa keeps of the brand. *2027 — the 27th Canadian Electrical Code:* its Section 64 storage rules and whether it references C800 directly. *Each large-scale fire test announced by a covered integrator:* which body witnesses it — a continued drift to TÜV Rheinland and UL would confirm Judgment 4. *The next C800 edition:* whether it is still a CSA/ANSI consensus document or is folded into UL 9540A. *Early 2028 — Brecksville completion:* whether Kiwa finishes the building on the announced footprint.
